chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Asam from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Zurara who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Durays had under his control the daughter of Humran, so he stipulated for her that he would never marry another woman over her, during her life and after her death. In return, she stipulated for him that she would not marry after him. They made upon both of them as a guarantee: Hajj, Umrah, offerings, vows, and all wealth they possess given to the poor, and every slave they own becomes free, if either one of them does not fulfill his obligation to the other. Then he came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and mentioned that to him. He said:

Indeed, her father Humran has a right (of choice/option), and that will not prevent us from telling you the truth. Go and marry and be content (with a single wife), for that is nothing (valid), and there is no penalty upon you nor upon her, and what you did is not invalid. So he married (her fully) and children were born to him after that.

key_terms.إِنَّ لِأَبِيهَا حُمْرَانَ حَقًّا: Indeed, her father Humran has a right
key_terms.ضُرَيْسًا: A female slave or concubine under ownership
key_terms.عَلَى أَنْ جَعَلَتْ لَهُ: On condition that she stipulated for him
key_terms.فَجَعَلَا عَلَيْهِمَا: They made upon both of them
key_terms.وَكُلُّ مَمْلُوكٍ لَهُمْ حُرٌّ: And every slave they own becomes free
key_terms.وَلَا ذَلِكَ الَّذِي صَنَعْتُمَا بِشَيْء: And what you did is not invalid
key_terms.وَلَا عَلَيْكَ شَيْءٌ: And there is no penalty upon you
key_terms.وَلَا يَحْمِلُنَا ذَلِكَ عَلَى أَنْ لَا: And that does not prevent us from telling you the truth
key_terms.وَوُلِدَ لَهُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَوْلَادٌ: And children were born to him after that

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on mutual exclusivity stipulations in Shia marriage contracts?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the stipulation of mutual exclusivity (*ta'kid al-nikah*) as a valid contractual condition that does not invalidate the marriage, reflecting the Shia principle that conditions not contrary to the essence of marriage are binding. The Imam’s ruling emphasizes that such stipulations serve as voluntary guarantees rather than absolute prohibitions, allowing the couple to remarry others if they choose, thereby highlighting the flexibility within Shia family law regarding marital agreements.
